tagline: Along the north shore of a lake the Navy listens to.
intro: From US 95 at Ponderay, Idaho 200 heads east along the rocky north shore of Lake Pend Oreille, at the feet of the Cabinet Mountains, through Kootenai, Hope and East Hope, with turnouts and overlooks along the way. Past the town of Clark Fork the lake gives out. The road follows the Clark Fork River up its valley to the Montana line.

The lake is the largest in Idaho and 1,152 feet deep in places, deep and quiet enough that the Navy still tests large-scale submarine prototypes in it. Its name is French for an ear pendant, after the ones the Kalispel wore. On a map the lake is shaped much like an ear.

moments.title: Hope
moments.text: A town of under a hundred people on the northeast shore of the lake, and the home of the artist Edward Kienholz.

moments.title: Clark Fork
moments.text: Named for William Clark, whose party probably met this river far upstream near Missoula, the railroad town kept a ferry in the 1890s that ran as far as Heron, Montana.

moments.title: Cabinet
moments.text: Just above the settlement of Cabinet, a concrete arch dam stands near where ancient ice dams held back Glacial Lake Missoula, and it went up in 1951 and 1952 in half the estimated time.

practical: Two-lane paved road with scenic turnouts. Expect ice and snow in winter.
